sources.title: Title 8, Chapter 5: Corporation Franchise Tax
sources.locator: 8 Del. C. § 502(a) (annual report on or before March 1; $200 late-filing penalty), § 504(a) (tax due and payable March 1; quarterly tentative installments when prior-year liability was $5,000 or more)
sources.note: Official online statutory text; verified live 2026-09-29 ('Annually on or before March 1' in § 502(a)). Check current text and session laws before relying on amounts.

sources.title: Annual Report Filing and Franchise Tax Payments (corp.delaware.gov/frtax)
sources.locator: Sections: 'Taxes and Annual Reports are to be received no later than March 1st of each year'; minimum tax $175 (authorized shares method) / $400 (assumed par value capital method); quarterly installments when owing $5,000+; mandated electronic filing for domestic corporations
sources.note: Agency filing instructions; amounts and thresholds change — recheck the live page before relying on figures.

sources.title: Instructions for Form 1120, U.S. Corporation Income Tax Return
sources.locator: When To File: 'a corporation must file its income tax return by the 15th day of the 4th month after the end of its tax year'; June 30 fiscal-year exception (15th day of the 3rd month); Saturday/Sunday/legal-holiday next-business-day rule; Form 7004 extensions
sources.note: Current-revision online instructions; verified live 2026-09-29. Recheck the live instructions for the applicable tax year before filing.

sources.title: Instructions for Form 941, Employer's QUARTERLY Federal Tax Return
sources.locator: When Must You File?: 'Your Form 941 is due by the last day of the month that follows the end of the quarter' (April 30 / July 31 / October 31 / January 31); timely-deposit 10-day extension; next-business-day rule
sources.note: Current-revision online instructions; verified live 2026-09-29. Deposit schedules (monthly/semiweekly) are a separate obligation from the quarterly return.

sources.publisher: United States Patent and Trademark Office
sources.title: Responding to office actions (trademarks)
sources.locator: 'What is a nonfinal versus a final office action?' — respond within three months from issue, optional three-month extension for a fee; Madrid Section 66(a): six months, no extension
sources.note: Agency guidance page, fetched live 2026-10-01 (the three-month and extension text verified verbatim). 37 CFR 2.62 and the TMEP control; recheck the live page and the office action itself before relying.
